tip.blitz: Attack: hit every blot you can and close your home board.

why.running_race: No contact is possible — it's a straight race to bear off ({{myPips}} vs {{foePips}} pips).

feedback.hint_nudge: Need a nudge? Look for the highlighted spots.

graduation.body: You know the goal, the board, how turns work, hitting, and bearing off. A quick check — then your first real game.
graduation.recap_2: Roll two dice; land on open points
graduation.recap_3: Hit blots → they sit on the bar
graduation.recap_4: Bear off only from your home board
graduation.recap_5: Games start with one die each — higher goes first (ties re-roll)
graduation.title: You’re ready to play

learn.home_cta_ready: You’re ready — play a real game

overshoot.body: Nothing is on the 5-point, but you rolled a 5. Bear off from your highest checker (the 3). A bigger number still takes a checker off.
overshoot.hint: Select point 3, then tap the bear-off tray.
overshoot.praise: That’s the overshoot rule — you’ll use it a lot when bearing off.
overshoot.title: Bigger die, still off

try.body: All your checkers are in home (1–6), so you can bear off. You rolled a 3 — take the checker on the 3-point off the board.
try.hint: Select point 3, then tap the bear-off area on the right edge.
try.praise: Off the board! First to bear off all 15 wins.
try.title: Bear one off

explain.body: The horseshoe matches the checkers of the player whose turn it is. It traces that player's route around the board and into home (points 1–6).
explain.title: The horseshoe path

far.body: Tap the point where your two farthest white checkers start (the 24-point, top-right).
far.hint: Look at the top-right — two white checkers on point 24.
far.praise: Those start deep in the opponent’s home and have the longest journey.
far.title: Your farthest checkers

home_stack.body: Tap the big stack of five white checkers already in your home (the 6-point).
home_stack.hint: Bottom-right: five white checkers on point 6.
home_stack.praise: That’s your home stack — five already waiting on the 6-point, closest to bearing off. Every game starts this way.
home_stack.title: Your home stack

bar.body: The raised strip in the middle is the bar. Hit checkers wait here. Tap the bar.
bar.hint: Tap the vertical strip between the left and right halves of the board.
bar.praise: Right — hit checkers sit on the bar until they re-enter.
bar.title: The bar

explain.body: You and your opponent each have 15 checkers. Move them around the board and off — first one finished wins.
explain.title: First to bear off wins

home.body: Your home is points 1–6 (bottom-right). Tap any point in your home board.
home.hint: Home is the six points in the bottom-right quadrant — numbered 1 through 6.
home.praise: That’s your home — checkers leave the board from here.
home.title: Find your home board

enter.body: You’re on the bar — come back on before moving anyone else. Count from the 24-point toward home: a 4 lands on point 21.
enter.hint: Tap the bar, then point 21 (not 23 — that’s only two pips from the bar).
enter.praise: You’re back on the board — bar checkers always enter first.
enter.title: Enter from the bar
enter.wrong: That’s only two pips from the bar (point 23). Count four points from 24 toward home — that’s point 21.

hit.body: A single checker is a blot. Land on it and it goes to the bar. You rolled a 3 — hit the black blot on the 5-point.
hit.hint: Tap your checker on 8, then tap point 5.
hit.praise: Hit! That black checker is now on the bar.
hit.title: Hit the blot

blocked.body: Two or more opponent checkers block a point — you can’t land there. Tap the blocked black stack on the 5-point.
blocked.hint: The highlighted stack of two black checkers on point 5.
blocked.praise: Right — a made point (2+) is closed. Empty, your own, or a blot (1) are open.
blocked.title: Blocked points

doubles.body: Doubles give you four moves of that number. You rolled 2-2 — that’s four 2s. Move from the 8-point to the 6-point four times.
doubles.hint: Tap the 8-point, then the 6-point. Do this four times — once per die.
doubles.praise: Exactly — doubles mean four moves with that number.
doubles.title: Doubles = four moves

explain.body: Each turn you roll two dice and play both numbers when you can. You may land on empty points, your own checkers, or a lone opponent (a blot).
explain.title: Two numbers, open points

two_dice.body: You rolled 3 and 1. Move the checker on the 8-point three pips (to 5), and the one on the 6-point one pip (to 5).
two_dice.hint: Select a white checker, then tap point 5. Do this for both the 8-point and the 6-point.
two_dice.praise: Nice — both dice used. Same checker or two checkers, both numbers must be played when you can.
two_dice.title: Play both dice

ahead.body: White has borne off 5 checkers and the rest are close to home. Black's checkers are still spread across the board. Tap any white checker — white is ahead in the race with the lower pip count.
ahead.hint: Look for the checkers closest to bearing off.
ahead.praise: Exactly! White's lower pip count means fewer points to travel.
ahead.title: Who's ahead?

behind.body: Same position. Black's checkers are far from home with a much higher pip count. Tap any black checker — black is behind in the race.
behind.hint: Look for the checkers farthest from home.
behind.praise: Right! Black needs many more pips to bear off.
behind.title: Who's behind?

explain.body: Pip count is the total number of points your checkers must travel to bear off. Each checker contributes its point number — a checker on the 6-point counts 6, on the 13-point counts 13. Add them all up and you get your pip count. Lower is better: it means you're closer to bearing off. The pip counts appear at the top of the screen during every game, with a dot showing which number belongs to which color.
explain.title: What is pip count?

pip_count.subtitle: Learn to read who's winning the race
pip_count.title: Pip Count: The Race Score

blitz.body: You have a strong home board and your opponent has blots or checkers on the bar. Attack! Hit every blot you can and close your home board points. The goal is to trap their checkers on the bar while you bear off. Here white has three home-board points made and black has a checker on the bar.
blitz.title: Blitz

identify.body: This is a priming game. Tap any point that's part of the white prime — the wall of consecutive made points blocking black.
identify.hint: Look for consecutive points with at least 2 white checkers each.
identify.praise: Perfect! That wall is the prime — black's back checkers are trapped.
identify.title: Spot the prime

prime.body: You've built a wall of consecutive made points — a prime. The highlighted points form a 4-point prime that restricts black's back checkers. Extend your prime one point at a time and trap their checkers behind it.
prime.title: Priming Game

running.body: You lead the race with no blots in hitting range. The plan is simple: bring your checkers home safely and avoid leaving blots. Don't get fancy — just run. This position shows white ahead in the race with a solid home board.
running.title: Running Game

bar.b: Enter that checker before moving anything else
bar.prompt: While you have a checker on the bar, you must…

bear.b: Only after you hit a blot
bear.c: When all 15 checkers are in your home board

blot.a: Any stack of three or more
blot.b: A single checker on a point — it can be hit
blot.c: Two or more checkers on a point — a made point

pip_ahead.a: Your opponent, with the higher count
pip_ahead.c: Neither — pip count doesn't measure the race
pip_ahead.prompt: Your pip count is 85 and your opponent's is 102. Who is ahead in the race?

pip_meaning.a: The total points your checkers must travel to bear off
pip_meaning.b: The number of checkers you have on the board
pip_meaning.c: The number of points you have made
pip_meaning.prompt: What does your pip count represent?

strat_blitz.a: Hit the blot and keep building your home board (blitz)
strat_blitz.b: Ignore the blot and run your back checkers
strat_blitz.c: Break your home board to make an anchor
strat_blitz.prompt: You have 3 home-board points made and your opponent has a blot in your home board. What's the best plan?

strat_prime.b: Keep the prime and extend it — they're trapped
strat_prime.c: Bear off as fast as possible
strat_prime.prompt: Your opponent has two checkers trapped behind your 5-point prime. What's your plan?
